paper_title: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource   Settings
caption: : Task-wise Class Distributions
model_annotation: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of classes across a multi-task benchmark for abusive language detection. The chart is composed of fifteen slices, each representing a different category of text. The largest slice, colored orange, is labeled “Positive” and appears to occupy approximately 30% of the total area. Following this is a slice labeled “Neutral,” colored beige, which accounts for approximately 20%.  The next largest segment, colored teal, is labeled “Negative,” representing approximately 18%.  Smaller slices are colored in varying shades of blue and green and labeled “Political,” “Religious,” “Abusive,” “Sexist,” “Racial,” “TiALD,” “Not Abusive,” “Mixed,” and “Other,” with the proportion of each slice visually estimated to be between 5% and 8%. A legend is provided to delineate the colors associated with each category.  The slices appear ordered from largest to smallest, moving clockwise from the “Positive” slice.
